ReAct is an international network which was created in 2005. It was one of the first organisations to articulate the complex nature of antibiotic resistance and its drivers, while calling for a holistic view of the problem and solutions that engage all segments of society. The core focus of ReAct's work is on developing sustainable solutions to tackle Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) in low and middle income countries (LMICs). AMR threatens the effective prevention and treatment of an ever-increasing range of infections caused by bacteria, parasites, viruses and fungi. WHO has declared that AMR is one of the top 10 global public health threats facing humanity (WHO, 2021, AMR Fact Sheet). ReAct aims to tackle AMR by influencing the policies and practices of international and non-governmental organisations, social movements, governments, the pharmaceutical industry and scientific, medical and local communities that grapple with the drivers and consequences of AMR. ReAct generates change through evidence-based advocacy, particularly by translating scientific evidence into policy, by sharing information generated through partnerships, pilots and programs. ReAct's Strategic Plan 2023 -2026 has three objectives; 1) GOVERNANCE & FUNDING of the work on antibiotic resistance. The overarching vision of ReAct is "A world free from untreatable infections" This is addressed through work on both equitable access and the risk that excess or inappropriate use of antibiotics leads to.
The contribution aims to support advancement of the three strategic objectives of ReAct's Strategic Plan 2023-2026, more specifically:
Strategic objective 1: Governance structures on antibiotic resistance including sufficient funding to implement national action plans, are transparent, accountable and responsive to LMIC needs; and have a framework in place to actively engage with civil society.
Strategic objective 2: A One Health approach is advanced to minimize spread of antibiotic resistance that is responsive to LMIC needs, and with a strong focus on national action plan implementation, health systems strengthening and community engagement.
Strategic objective 3: A public health driven approach for development and delivery of new antibiotics and diagnostics, and where access for people in LMICs is central, will take stronger root among governments and international institutions
Critical Enabler: Community and civil society mobilization is critical for strong and sustainable action on antibiotic resistance.

.ReAct's narrativa årsrapport för år 2025 redogör för att AMR frågor i högre grad har kunnat förankrats i konkreta frågor som lagstiftning, utvecklingen av nationella livsmedelssystem, utbildning och internationella ramverk för forskning och innovation. ReAct lyfter hur deras samarbeten utanför hälsosektorn, genom deras arbete med fokus på civilsamhället, kopplingar till trosbaserade organisationer, lantbrukare och konstnärer, liksom till tematiska områden som WASH, miljö och OneHealth har bidragit till detta skifte att konkretisera AMR i vardagsfrågor kopplade till sociala verkligheter och närmiljö, istället för att definieras som en strikt teknisk fråga. ReAct bedömer att detta skapar förutsättningar för långsiktiga resultat.
Rapporten redogör vidare för utförda aktiviteter och vad detta lett till både på kort och längre sikt. Bland annat noteras hur engagemang för unga stärkts genom aktiviteter närmare kopplade till politiska processer samt hur beaktandet av traditionella könsroller och jämställdhet spelar in i verksamhet som bedrivs av civilsamhället, mycket tack vare ReActs arbete.
Sammantaget var enligt ReAct några av de viktigaste lärdomarna under 2025 vikten av långsiktigt och uthålligt arbete för att uppnå policyförändringar, behovet av starkare regionala samordningsstrukturer samt betydelsen av lokalt ägarskap för relevans och hållbarhet. Finansiell osäkerhet och minskad global hälsobiståndsfinansiering identifierades som växande utmaningar för genomförandet och den långsiktiga planeringen.
I slutet av år 2024 lät ReAct på uppdrag av Sida genomföra en extern utvärdering av ReActs verksamhet. Utvärderingen syftade främst till att bedöma verksamhetens relevans, effektivitet, resurseffektivitet, påverkan och hållbarhet, samt i vilken utsträckning verksamheten bidrar till långsiktiga och bestående resultat.
En central del av utvärderingen har ambitionen att besvara frågan " i vilken utsträckning har verksamheten haft effekt?" Utvärderingen var dock en halvtidsutvärdering och tittade därför på tidiga tecken på "impact" som genereras ur ReAct's verksamhet åren 2023-2024. Nedan ett par exempel på "tidiga exempel på impact":
The evaluation identifies five main areas where ReAct has made meaningful progress:
1. Contributions to Global and Regional AMR Policy Processes
ReAct played a significant role in shaping the policy framing ahead of the 2024 UN High-Level Meeting on Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), ensuring that themes like equitable access, prevention, and community perspectives were included in the final declaration. The organization provided expert input to WHO-led policy processes on gender, equity, people-centered approaches, and National Action Plan (NAP) implementation, which were incorporated into policy documents. ReActs positions influenced debates on incentives, stewardship, and access in the EU pharmaceutical legislation process, and supported Africa CDCs development of a continental AMR framework.
2. Strengthening National AMR Governance Structures
ReActs support helped establish and consolidate national AMR coordination mechanisms in countries such as Zambia, Kenya, and Malawi. These committees now have clearer mandates, regular technical working groups, and, in some cases, dedicated staff, and are embedded in government systems. Revisions and development of NAPs in several African countries and sub-national planning models in India and Kenya have improved countries ability to coordinate and implement AMR responses.
3. Improvements in Antimicrobial Stewardship Practices
ReAct contributed to early improvements in antimicrobial stewardship in health facilities, particularly in Zambia and Kenya. Stewardship teams were established or strengthened, leading to more structured prescribing practices and greater adherence to treatment guidelines. There was a reported shift toward increased use of first-line antibiotics and more restrictive use of broad-spectrum classes, indicating emerging improvements in clinical practice.
4. Increased Capacity and Engagement of Stakeholder Groups
Capacity-building activities across Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America led to stronger awareness and technical competence among government officials, civil society organizations, youth groups, and educators. Trained actors, such as youth groups in Kenya and educators in Latin America, continued to engage in AMR activities independently, suggesting the formation of new actors able to support AMR efforts over time.
5. Strengthened Organisational Capacity
ReAct expanded its staffing, improved coordination through the Global Leadership Group, and increased its visibility and recognition among governments, multilateral agencies, and civil society. These developments position the network to better influence policy processes, support implementation, and sustain engagement with key stakeholder.
Ovan resultat utgör betydelsefulla framsteg mot de övergripande förändringar som anges i ReActs strategiska plan.
Framöver kommer förmågan att prioritera insatser, säkerställa resultatens långsiktiga hållbarhet och stärka organisationens interna system att vara avgörande för att omvandla dessa tidiga framsteg till varaktig förändring.
Bland de oväntade resultaten märks att ReActs modeller har spridits till nya länder och sektorer samt att nya ledare inom AMR-arbetet har vuxit fram. Begränsande faktorer har varit politiska hinder, resursbrist och samordningsutmaningar, både internt och externt.
